recipes.name: Easy Apple Dumplings
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) can refrigerated flaky biscuit dough

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Butter a 7 x 11-inch baking pan. Separate dough into 8 pieces; flatten each into a circle. Wrap one biscuit around each apple half; place in the pan, seam-side down.
Combine sugar, water, butter, and vanilla extract in a small bowl. Pour mixture over dumplings; sprinkle with cinnamon. Bake until golden, 35 to 40 minutes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Apple Dumplings
raw_recipe.description: This easy apple dumplings recipe makes sweet biscuit-wrapped apples that float in a buttery vanilla and cinnamon sauce. Delicious with ice cream.

review.reviewBody:
OMG, this is one of the best dessert recipes I have ever tried! Thankfully, I read each and every review before trying them. Please, people, do make the recommended adjustments and I promise you will not be disappointed!

I diced the apples and coated them with cinnamon/sugar. I baked the dumplings on one side for 20 minutes. Then I turned them and baked for another 10 minutes before adding the sauce. I made up the sauce minus the water and had to add just a tablespoon or so to get it the right consistency. I also used 1/2 white sugar and 1/2 brown sugar and ended up with this beautiful caramel sauce. I added the sauce the last 10 minutes of cooking and served with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. 

I had people begging me for the recipe and I have made it twice this week. My husband has requested that this be THE dessert for Thanksgiving dinner and I will be only to happy to oblige. Folks, it really is awesome!

This is just too good to be true. It was easy to prepare. I did follow the advice of the others by using only a little water and by cutting my apples into quarters. I used gala apples. I also sprinkled the apples with a little cinnamon and sugar before wrapping them with the croissant dough. And I baked for about 5 minutes before adding the liquid mixture and I used half brown sugar half white sugar. These were sooooooooooooooooooooooo good. You must eat it with vanilla ice cream. I am going to make another batch today.

These were ah-mazing!!! I followed other reviewers suggestions and used half brown sugar ans only a few tablespoons of water for the sauce. Cubed up the apple and mixed it with sugar and cinnamon (really a must for any baked apple recipe). BAKED seam down for 20 minutes then flipped, after another 10 minutes added the sauce and then cooked for the last 10 minutes. Also, I used the phillsberry apple turnover dough and because they are cut as squares and I tried to reshape them, they got incredibly thin. This was the best serendipitous event: as they tore at the bottom of the pan the glaze hardened over them. Once they were cooked you got a nice semi-transparent sauce with little sneak peak of the apple chunks. Everyone raved about them and said they loved the taste of the dough. All in all, a great recipe with some minor mods.

I also cut my apples into chunks and added sugar and cinnamon before putting them in the biscuit. I also added a pat of butter before closing them up. I used the water, sugar and cinnamon mixture the way the recipe called for. My family raved about them. I would have included a picture but they were gone before I thought about taking one. 😊

I make mine differently and it's faster. Instead of biscuits I use crescent rolls. I separate the dough, instead of tearing into triangles I leave them in rectangles, each can yields 4 dumplings. You need 2 cans of crescent rolls. I chop my apples to place in the dough and in a saucepan I combine 1 3/4 cup water 1 cup of sugar and cinnamon you can adjust to your taste. You can sprinkle cinnamon on top of dumplings or add to saucepan you also need 1 stick of butter to saucepan. Pour over dumplings and bake at 350 degrees until golden brown,

I made this using the suggestions posted. I cubed the apples and sprinkled with cinnamon and sugar per my tastes. I baked at 350 degrees for 20 minutes. While the dumplings baked, I prepared the syrup. The syrup part: 1/4 cup water, 1/2 cup each of white and brown sugar, 1/2 cup butter and the 2 tsp of vanilla. I cooked the liquid on top of the stove over low heat and brought it to a boil. This helps to dissolve the sugar. After the 20 minutes baking time, I removed the dumplings from the oven and poured the syrup around the edges. I sprinkled a bit more cinnamon on top of the dumplings and returned them to the oven to bake another 13 minutes. Delicious! This is an easy recipe and one to take on a camping trip or vaction at the beach when I don't want to drag a whole lot of ingredients.

ALL-TIME FAVORITE! I used butter-flavored Grands Biscuits. Sprinkle your sliced apples AND the biscuits with cinnamon/sugar. To avoid the "soggy bottom," I melted just enough butter to lightly cover the bottom of my baking dish and baked the dumplings (without the syrup) for about 20 minutes. Then, I poured 1/2 the syrup over the top of the dumplings and finished baking---about another 25 minutes. Use the remaining syrup to glaze the dumplings when they are done baking or save for serving time. When making the syrup, I used the hint to add-in just enough liquid (water, OJ, mountain dew) to achieve the desired consistency. These dumplings were picture perfect--tender, flavorful apples, sweet syrup and no soggy dough. Simply delicious and do not forget the ice cream!

Absolutely wonderful recipe! My husband whose favorite dessert is peach or apple cobbler has declared this as its replacement. I have made these almost every weekend since we found this recipe. I too followed the recommendation of other reviewers: reduced water to 1/4 cup, cut apples in wedges before wrapping with dough and covered with cinnamon/sugar mixture. I used 1/2 jazz apples and 1/2 granny smith and found that while the flavor was the same with both the jazz apples maintained their shape better and the granny smith cooked down to almost nothing, but both were fabulous! Also I made 1/2 with crescent dough and 1/2 with ready made crusts and hands down everyone thought the ones with the crescent dough were better. I also added nutmeg before pouring on the sauce. The last time I made them I didn't bother peeling the apples and it didn't seem to make any difference. Do yourself a favor and make this dish...next time will try reducing the butter because I don't think it will affect the flavor that much.

I made the recipe, as is, the first time, decreasing the water to 1/2-cup. I did sprinkle the apples with cinnamon, sugar & a pinch of nutmeg. 

However, I got a brainstorm for the second time around...

Instead of canned biscuits I used canned cinnamon rolls instead. I used 1/2-cup orange juice in place of the water. (I didn't use the glaze in the can, but you could.l I also added raisins & chopped walnuts. Those suckers were DIVINE!

Turned out great, but I edited the recipe. 
1. Add cinnamon sugar to the apple before wrapping
2. Sprinkled the top of the dumplings with a cinnamon sugar mix
3. Add extra vanilla and sugar before boiling to make a thicker mixture
With edits of other reviewers, (dice apples, no water to sauce, and bake 20 minutes on one side, 10 on the other)- Husbands new favorite.

I only used a 1/2 cup of water to give it a glazed cover. I put the apple halves in a bag with cinnamon sugar and coated them before enrobing them in the rolled out biscuits. Next time I will do a scratch dough in lieu of the biscuit dough and will cut the apples up to get a better bake on them.

I followed all the suggestions in the comments. Everything was great except for the sauce. I cooked them for 20 minutes then added the sauce and cooked for another 20 minutes. The sugar butter sauce was still grainy and never dissolved to make a smooth sauce. Next time I might try cooking the sauce first then adding in.

I usually use the Crescent Rolls. But had the Grands. Excellent recipe. With absolutely no effort. I didn't change any ingredients EXCEPT my Child wanted to add golden raisins. I did. Thank you for this tecipe☺️
I have made this many times over the years. Glad I found this recipe so I don't have to find mine. It is a great hit with the family and requested quit often. This is the exact recipe that I use!
chopped apples and put cinnamon and sugar on them. Next time use 1/2 brown sugar in sauce. I cooked 5 minutes first
I used crescent rolls and sliced the apples...Delicious
I forgot to add the sugar to the butter mixture so I sprinkled it over the apples while baking. Not bad!
